terms.gloss: safety, preservation; the safety of a state
evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.51: in optimōrum cōnsiliīs posita est cīvitātium salūs
terms.comment: salūs pūblica, the public safety; salūs reī pūblicae, the safety of the state.

evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.169: incolumitās est salūtis tūta atque integra cōnservātiō (Lewis & Short)
Suet. Tib. 37.1: tuendae pācis ā grassātūrīs ac latrōciniīs
M-O s.v. public safety or security

terms.gloss: freedom from care; after Augustus, safety, security
terms.comment: In Cicero a mind free from care; the sense safety comes after Augustus, and modern Latin uses it for security, as in the police’s pūblicae sēcūritātis custōdēs.

phrases.latin: certē in optimōrum cōnsiliīs posita est cīvitātium salūs
phrases.english: surely the security of states lies in the counsels of the best men

phrases.latin: vix mī ipse crēdēns Thȳniam atque Bīthȳnōs līquisse campōs et vidēre tē in tūtō
phrases.english: hardly believing that I have left Thynia and the Bithynian plains and see you in safety

phrases.latin: in prīmīs tuendae pācis ā grassātūrīs ac latrōciniīs sēditiōnumque licentiā cūram habuit
phrases.english: above all he took care to keep the peace against footpads, robbery and lawless riots
